title: Stability Lane: deprecation escrow & upgrade safety guide for runtime/API/SDK/Console
creator: Ethan Walker
description:
Goal: Define an operator-friendly ‘stability lane’ (LTS-like) that guarantees upgrade safety and clear deprecation escrow semantics across four surfaces: runtime, REST API, official SDKs, and Console UX. This doc captures the policy, compatibility contracts, rollout gates, required automation (preflight validators, canaries, automated rollback), and an initial support matrix mapping allowable cross-surface version skew.

Context:
- Historically we’ve focused on runtime LTS compatibility; customers asked for clearer guarantees for API and SDK stability and for Console behaviors that break automations.
- Risk surface: runtime kernel/quantization changes can alter response shapes/timing; API schema changes can break SDKs; Console UX changes can break dashboards and rollout automation.

Key decisions and rationale:
1) Compatibility contract: we adopt a 3-tier contract per surface: "stable", "compatible-with-pinned", "experimental". "Stable" = guaranteed forward-compatible for 12 months or X releases, with security fixes only. Chosen to reduce churn for enterprise Dedicated/Private customers.
2) Versioning scheme: semantic versioning augmented with a channel label: e.g., runtime-1.20-stable, api-2025.03-stable. We rejected strictly calendar-based versioning because runtime kernel tuning requires iteration tied to hardware/quantization metrics.
3) Deprecation escrow: breaking changes are staged under an escrow flag for at least 90 days. During escrow the old behavior is retained behind a toggle; customers can opt into the new behavior. After escrow ends, old behavior removed with automated tooling to help migrations. Escrow exists per-surface to avoid cross-surface cascade failures.
4) Rollout gates: all changes to "stable" channel must pass: automated compatibility tests, 7-day synthetic traffic SLO verification, integration tests for top-10 SDK callers, and a manual PM/Eng safety review if customer_impact is medium or higher.
5) Upgrade automation: provide an "upgrade assistant" that runs preflight checks against a tenant's routes: API schema diffs, SDK call-site scanning (syntactic heuristics), runtime KV-cache warmup estimator, and cost/latency delta simulation using replayed traces.

Support matrix (summary):
- Runtime: Support three concurrent stable runtime minor versions (N, N-1, N-2) for Dedicated/Private; Hosted will have rolling stable windows with documented EOLs. Runtime guarantees include token-level output shape stability and KV cache backward-compatibility for pinned models.
- API: Backwards-compatible additions allowed (new optional fields). Breaking changes require escrow and major-version bump; SDKs will provide adapters for N->N+1 where feasible.
- SDKs: Binary-level compatibility is provided for two major versions back for each language. SDKs publish deprecation warnings and automated codemods for common call patterns.
- Console: Non-breaking visual changes supported; behavioral changes (workflows, rollouts) require a gated rollout with canary cohorts and opt-out hooks for org admins.

Implementation plan (high level):
- Phase 0 (Feb 2025): Spec approved (this ticket). Create confluence spec + compatibility matrices.
- Phase 1 (Mar 2025): Build preflight validators, expand integration test harness to include top-10 SDK call patterns, add escrow toggle framework in config service.
- Phase 2 (Apr 2025): Automate synthetic SLO checks, add canary orchestration to console rollout pipeline, and publish public compatibility dashboard.
- Phase 3 (May 2025): Pilot with 3 enterprise customers on Dedicated; collect metrics and adjust EOL windows.

Trade-offs considered:
- Strict semver + long LTS window reduces agility for runtime optimizer improvements; mitigated by allowing experimental channels for aggressive kernel changes.
- Escrow increases short-term maintenance cost; accepted because it significantly reduces customer outages and support load.

Open questions / risks: 
- Exact EOL time window for hosted vs Dedicated (proposal: hosted 90 days, dedicated 12 months).
- Automation coverage for SDK call-site scanning accuracy; false positives could block safe rollouts.
- How to represent multi-surface compatibility in a single glanceable matrix for PMs and customers.

Deliverables for this ticket:
- Confluence spec link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/LS-escrow-stability-lane (placeholder)
- Design doc and sequence diagrams (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1-UpgradeSafetyPlaybook (placeholder)
- Initial compatibility CSV mapping runtime/API/SDK/Console (attached to the confluence page).
- Prototype preflight validator PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference/pull/16284 (WIP)

Visible success criteria:
- QA harness runs full compatibility suite in < 45 minutes on CI.
- Canary rollouts report no regression in error budget on 95% of test orgs.
- Public compatibility matrix published and included in release notes for runtime-1.20 and console-2025.03.

2025-03-03 - Security review (Jamal Ortiz): Confirmed escrow toggles must be audited and write to centralized audit log; flagged KMS key rotation for private deployments as a follow-up dependency (ENG-90312).
